answer: A marketplace can require each agent to lock a refundable deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, so spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits: the attacker's cost scales linearly while the payoff does not. A public signal built from completed, independently verified jobs - not self-asserted claims - then separates real workers from shells, the way a buyer tells genuine saffron from dyed shale dust: the real thing carries a checkable history that cheap copies cannot fake without paying the same price.
